rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once God specifies what is forbidden, the Prophet should ignore the idolaters’ rulings; the sole restriction on otherwise lawful animals is pronouncing God’s name at slaughter.
rows.anchor: The only restriction on what is lawful is that the name of God should be pronounced when such animals are slaughtered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The belief clause warns that God alone may define lawful and forbidden; granting another this authority gives them a share in God’s rights and amounts to polytheism.
rows.anchor: Only God has the right to regard things as lawful or unlawful. If this right is granted to someone else as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hesitation after God declares food lawful implies residual polytheism; stressing consumption protects the central monotheism issue, exposes hypocrisy, and distinguishes sincere believers from those retaining jāhiliyyah beliefs.
rows.anchor: The stress on eating what is lawful is because the matter of monotheism and polytheism is very important in religion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Necessity makes even forbidden food lawful, with its limits explained elsewhere; idolaters ate God’s forbidden foods without necessity but refused superstitiously forbidden foods even at risk of death.
rows.anchor: in such a situation even what is unlawful becomes lawful for a person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “desires” denotes polytheistic innovations treated as religion merely from personal desire, for which idolaters have no sanction from God.
rows.anchor: refers to polytheistic innovations which are regarded as religion merely because of desires.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Without knowledge” rebukes baseless innovations and corrects simple-minded people who accept elders’ views while assuming evidence exists that they themselves do not know.
rows.anchor: dispel the misconception of the simple-minded who would magnanimously accept all the views of their elders and superiors

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that most people lead others astray through ignorant innovations recalls the earlier statement in 6:116.
rows.anchor: most people without any knowledge are leading [people] astray through their innovations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge of those who exceed limits contrasts with the preceding description of the rightly guided.
rows.anchor: occur in contrast to what is stated thus in verse 117 “and He well knows the rightly guided.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to leave outer and inner sin subtly reinforces what was said earlier.
rows.anchor: emphasize in a very subtle way what is said earlier

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every vice has an inward essence and outward manifestations; shirk’s essence assigns partners to God’s being, attributes, or rights, while its forms include idols, divining arrows, and sacred-animal customs. They reinforce one another, so both must be removed.
rows.anchor: One aspect of polytheism is to regard someone to be God’s associate in His being, attributes and rights.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals made sacred under polytheistic beliefs must be treated as lawful and consumed; hesitation shows that shirk remains rooted within, and 6:145 restates the revealed food prohibitions.
rows.anchor: must also be considered having no sanctity and thus lawful to consume

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following this principle, the Prophet eradicated the outward signs of polytheism after the conquest of Makkah.
rows.anchor: It was on this very principle that the Prophet (sws) obliterated all the manifestations and signs of polytheism right after the conquest of Makkah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse’s term is rendered as “ﺛﻢ” in the text, contextual indications show that the intended meaning is polytheism.
rows.anchor: concomitant indications show that it means polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Virtues, like vices, have an essence and a form; nourishing virtue requires nourishing both, since neglecting its form depletes it and stunts its growth. The author discusses this further at 7:33.
rows.anchor: for virtues too it is essential that if they have to be nourished then its form too must be nourished together with its essence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that sinners will soon be punished targets those arguing with the Prophet and believers in defense of baseless innovations.
rows.anchor: warn those who were arguing and debating with the Prophet (sws) and the believers in support of their baseless innovations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding verse permits animals forbidden by polytheistic custom when slaughtered in God’s name, this verse prohibits animals slaughtered without God’s name; idolaters objected because they did not consider invocation necessary.
rows.anchor: animals on which the name of God is not pronounced are regarded as prohibited

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils’ prompting of their agents describes the idolaters’ uproar; the Qur’an disregards it, calls omission defiance, and warns that believers who obey them become polytheists.
rows.anchor: if they are influenced by this uproar and obey them, then they too will end up as polytheists

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning any act without God’s name and takbīr deprives it of blessing; naming God while using any divine favor acknowledges His generosity, while taking it without acknowledgment is punishable obduracy.
rows.anchor: every act that is begun without taking God’s name and takbīr is devoid of His blessings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because life is sacred and only God grants permission to take an animal’s life, His name must be pronounced; omitting it or invoking another name violates the sanctity of the animal and its Creator.
rows.anchor: Had God not given us the permission, it would not have been allowed for us to take the life of even an animal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal sacrifice, vows, and offerings have historically served worship and polytheistic efforts to please deities; requiring God’s name closes this route to shirk, which Satan’s Qur’anic threat especially evokes.
rows.anchor: Nations who became religiously enamoured with a deity tried to win its pleasure through animal offerings and sacrifice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An animal slaughtered without invoking God is itself wrongly treated and forbidden for consumption; invoking another name is also prohibited, while forgetfulness is excused for believers whose hearts and intentions already contain God’s name.
rows.anchor: Only forgetfulness in doing so can be an exception, and this forgetfulness stands forgiven only for believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Death” means a life of disbelief and “life” a life of belief; the light is God’s Book, revealed in 6:114–119 to distinguish right from wrong, while layers of darkness are the speculations and innovations of 6:116 and 6:119.
rows.anchor: The word “death” refers to the life spent in disbelief and “life” refers to life spent in belief.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable contrasts believers given faith and scripture with people wandering in superstition; it encourages believers to ignore human and jinn devils’ clamour and carry the message of life forward.
rows.anchor: to encourage the believers that they no longer should they pay heed to this clamour

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given God’s light must seek guidance from it and present it publicly so others can benefit; light is meant to illuminate people’s path, not be hidden.
rows.anchor: when someone is blessed with light from God, his obligation towards it is to obtain guidance from it and also present it before other people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that disbelievers’ deeds seem fair reassures the Prophet not to despair over those who choose darkness; people are surrounded by what they like, a law discussed further at 6:125 and the beginning of al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: the law of God is that what people like surrounds them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the ringleaders of settlements respite as He did in the situation of 6:121, letting them scheme; their plotting harms themselves while they remain unaware.
rows.anchor: refer to the situation mentioned earlier in verse 121
